rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round shifts weights toward stronger obfuscation while keeping costs moderate. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain because this program's small control-flow-heavy functions (main at 308 bytes, FSM state-transition logic) are ideal flattening targets that destroy cfg-based analysis cheaply. SUB stays high since arithmetic substitution is nearly free on a 1399-byte text segment and compounds well with FLA. BCF is raised to add opaque-predicate bogosity on top of flattened dispatch loops, but its RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights stay moderate so it applies selectively rather than everywhere. SPLIT keeps basic blocks fragmented to feed FLA more material at negligible cost. IBR and ICALL are elevated to obscure the call/branch graph (indirect dispatch hides the FSM transition table), with ICALL's CorrectnessRisk kept slightly elevated since indirect calls on C++ constructors/destructors (the duplicated C1/C2 pairs) carry the most semantic risk. IGV remains a moderate supplementary pass for global-variable indirection. No pass is disabled since round 0 showed the toolchain tolerates the full pipeline on this sample.
